follow_up_publications.title: Final overall survival and long-term safety results from the PRIMA/ENGOT-OV26/GOG-3012 trial

reviewed_evidence.design: Randomized, double-blind, phase III, placebo-controlled; 733 randomized 2:1 (niraparib n=487; placebo n=246).
reviewed_evidence.population: Newly diagnosed stage III–IV high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal carcinoma; complete/partial response after 6–9 cycles of first-line platinum chemotherapy; HRD defined by deleterious BRCA mutation and/or myChoice GIS ≥42.
reviewed_evidence.intervention: Oral niraparib once daily for up to 36 months or progression; initial 300 mg daily, amended individualized starting dose 200 mg if baseline weight <77 kg and/or platelets <150,000/mm³.
reviewed_evidence.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival hierarchically tested in HRD and overall populations.
reviewed_evidence.efficacy: HRD median PFS 21.9 vs 10.4 months (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.31–0.59; p<0.001); overall median PFS 13.8 vs 8.2 months (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.50–0.76; p<0.001). Final OS analysis: HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.84–1.23; p=0.8834); 5-year PFS 22% vs 12% overall and 35% vs 16% in HRD.
reviewed_evidence.safety: Grade ≥3 anemia 31.0%, thrombocytopenia 28.7%, neutropenia 12.8%; thrombocytopenia led to discontinuation in 4.3%; primary publication reports no decrement in patient-reported quality of life. Long-term MDS/AML approximately 2.3% vs 1.6%.
reviewed_evidence.nnt: Landmark PFS: 5-year overall-population difference 10 percentage points (22−12), NNT 10; HRD difference 19 points (35−16), NNT 6. These are Kaplan–Meier landmark estimates, not crude event-count NNTs.

open_items.absolute_effect: 5-year PFS: 22% vs 12% overall (NNT 10); HRD subgroup 35% vs 16% (NNT 6).
